# Draft:Cold War 1994 (film)

----

| writer         = Longman Leung

Cold War 1994 is an upcoming Hong Kong police procedural action thriller film written and directed by Longman Leung. The film is a prequel to Cold War and Cold War 2 and the third installment in the Cold War film series. It features an ensemble cast starring Terrance Lau, Daniel Wu, Wu Kang-ren, Louis Koo, Tse Kwan-ho, Louise Wong, and also featuring Aaron Kwok, Tony Leung Ka-fai and Chow Yun-fat (reprising their roles from previous films). Like its title, the film is set in 1994, and deals with M.B. Lee's early career in the police force before he becomes deputy commissioner in the present day storyline.
The film is scheduled to release in 2026, and will be followed by a sequel, Cold War 1995.
Premise
In 2017, a few years after the events of Cold War 2, M.B. Lee, the former Deputy Commissioner of Police, suddenly goes disappearing, while former Police Commissioner Peter Choi is secretly assassinated in the UK. HKPF Commissioner Sean Lau investigates and seeks help from legislator and experienced barrister Oswald Kan to assist him in reopening the truth of a case from 1994 that may solve Lee's disappearance.
The main story is set in 1994 (3 years prior to the Hong Kong handover) during colonial British Hong Kong rule, where the Special Branch unit is about to dissolve, and the Hong Kong Police Force is preparing to undergo major restructures. During this time, a wealthy business tycoon is kidnapped that shakes the financial market. The investigation is spearheaded by OCTB  superintendent M.B Lee, who leads the case. During Lee's investigation, he comes across with Peter Choi, his senior colleague known for using calculating and cold tactics, leading both men to clash with internal politics and differing views.
As Lee continues to investigate deeper, he discovers the case involves multiple parties not only including the triads, but also the MI6, the elite circles as well as the police force itself. Faced with further external pressures, Lee must cross lines and strive to discover the truth.
Cast
* Terrance Lau as M.B. Lee (young), a courageous and righteous superintendent of OCTB (Organized Crime and Triad Bureau) in 1994.
* Daniel Wu as Peter Choi-Yuen-kei(young), the acting police commissioner in 1994, known for his cold and ruthless demeanor.
* Tony Leung Ka-fai as M.B. Lee (old), retired Deputy Commissioner of Police (Operations) who disappears in 2017 and a crucial character for the events of the Cold War films.
* Aaron Kwok as Sean Lau Kit-fai, the current Commissioner of Police who investigates a 1994 case (special appearance).
* Chow Yun-fat as Oswald Kan, an experienced senior barrister and legislator who assists Sean Lau in solving the 1994 case (special appearance).
* Louis Koo as Yip Shun-ting：The current 5th Chief Executive of Hong Kong in 2017 (special appearance).
* Tse Kwan-ho as Poon Shun-hang, a wealthy Hong Kong business tycoon who hails from the fourth generation heir of the Poon family.
* Wu Kang-ren as Poon Chi-ong, The fifth generation heir of the Poon family and Shun-hang's son.
* Louise Wong as Yuen Yeuk-lan, The leader of one of Hong Kong's biggest triads.
* Fish Liew as Rosamund Keswick Poon Yi-shum, a fourth generation descendant of the Poon family.
* Aidan Gillen as F.M, the MI6 branch leader in Asia's sector
* Hugh Bonneville as Whitehall, the British Secretary of State who represents the United Kingdom and is involved in Hong Kong's affairs.
Production
Development and filming
Since the release of Cold War 2  in 2016, there had not been any news of a sequel moving forward. Producer Bill Kong explained that the age of streaming services and constant reruns on film and television has led to a continued popularity of the Cold War film series, as both were box office hits when they came out. Kong and director Longman Leung came to agreement working on the film after Leung had completed Anita, which was released in 2021.
Leung has stated the ideas of a prequel had been planted in the first film, in which M.B. Lee is interrogated by a ICAC senior officer (played by Aarif Rahman), who questions the latter that he "had planned a perfect undercover operation in 1995 that dismantled an entire triad organization", and this line of dialogue was the perfect starting point for a prequel, including allusions of Lee's past in the second film as well.
The film began development in 2024, as the production team choose to utilise 1994 as its contemporary setting, due to the Special Branch's dissolvement under colonial British era rule, while the Hong Kong Police Force was undergoing major changes before the handover in 1997; these circumstances back then also affected the British government, triad circles, and the wealthy elite that provided much backdrop for the film's story. The film is meant to be set up as Lee's origin story and his early days of foray in his police career. Filming took place in early 2024 for the span of 5 months, with scenes mainly shot in Hong Kong and partially London.
Casting
Terrance Lau, Daniel Wu and Wu Kang-ren were cast in 2024, while Carlos Chan was revealed to be also attached to the project. A major selling theme was passing down the torch, as Lau portrays a younger M.B. Lee in his early years. During the movie launch event, Tony Leung gave his blessing and handling the mantle over of his role, noting Lau's versatility and praised his acting abilities. The film also marks Daniel Wu's six year return to Hong Kong films after Caught in Time. It is noted the film casted a handful of British and Irish actors, including renowned actors Aiden Gillen and Hugh Bonneville  which sets the film's tone of international and political realism.
Release
The film's poster was first shown at the 2025 Cannes Film Festival's Hong Kong Cinema panel, followed by a 15 second teaser released in June at the Shanghai International Film Festival. On March 18 2026, a movie event panel part of Entertainment Expo Hong Kong took place at the HKCEC, revealing its main full cast of 12 actors and synopsis. The event was attended by director Longman Leung, producers Bill Kong and Ivy Ho, film stars Terrance Lau, Louise Wong, Tse Kwan-ho and Tony Leung. The film is scheduled to be released sometime in 2026, with an unspecified date to be announced.
Sequel
Cold War 1994 was shot back-to-back with its sequel, Cold War 1995.  Both films were shot during early 2024, mainly in Hong Kong and also London. Cold War 1995 will continue the story of Cold War 1994, dealing with the aftermath of the kidnapping case in 1994, with the arrival of MI6 in Hong Kong to deal with affairs, and M.B. Lee's protection of an informant that complicates further matters. It is predicted to release in the fiscal year of 2027.
